findings.claim: ADR-0015 lists `flood-guard.ts` under DELETE with no v2 successor named anywhere. This file is not output-size capping (ADR-0016/ADR-0008); it is a separate fix for #769, a per-agent-context rolling-window call-rate throttle on ctx_search so that N concurrent subagents (the owner's own '10 agents' plan) are not summed into one global budget and wrongly blocked.
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY. INTRODUCED_BY: 3a45eb1c 'fix(search): correct project-filter strictness (#827) + per-agent flood-guard (#769)' (2026-06-21), adding src/search/flood-guard.ts, src/server.ts wiring, src/session/db.ts, and two test files. ORIGINAL_INTENT (file header comment, src/search/flood-guard.ts:1-21): 'Issue #769: a parallel multi-agent fan-out (Claude Code Task/Workflow) runs N subagents concurrently against the SAME per-session MCP server process. With a single global counter their independent calls are summed into one budget, so legitimate fan-out ("10 agents x 2 calls") trips the guard that was only ever meant to catch ONE actor spamming... the counter must be keyed per agent-context -- NOT removed.' ADR-0016 (subagent-context-protection.md) covers a different axis entirely: the byte size of one tool output landing in a subagent's context, not the call-rate budget across concurrent subagents calling ctx_search. No ADR, no TECH-SPEC line, and no entry in REVIEW-r4a/ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r4/BOTTLENECKS-r4 reassigns this behavior. grep across those three files for '769' or 'flood' returns nothing.
findings.fix: Either name the v2 module that keeps a per-agent-context keyed rolling-window throttle on ctx_search (reusing src/search/flood-guard.ts's design, not a global counter), or explicitly state in ADR-0015/ADR-0016 that call-rate throttling is dropped for v2 and why concurrent subagent fan-out (10 agents) will not re-trip a single global counter. Add a GP case replaying #769 (N concurrent subagents, legitimate fan-out, must not block).

findings.claim: VERDICT for ADR-0006: ACCEPT AS PROPOSED, pending the r3-ordered re-probe. This ADR covers a 2026 Claude Code platform feature (tool search / alwaysLoad) with no v1 code path to archaeology against -- v1 never had tool search deferral, so there is no prior fix or regression to re-break.
findings.evidence: Searched cm-main (2230-commit history) for the probed mechanism: `git log --all -S 'alwaysLoad'` and `git log --all -S 'ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH'` return no commits. This feature postdates v1's entire commit range, so GIT ARCHAEOLOGY correctly finds nothing to cite -- there is no REGRESSION_RISK category here because there is no prior v1 behavior being kept, changed or dropped. The ADR's own open item, Q19 ('re-probe alwaysLoad on Opus and Sonnet in the keyless harness before Accepted'), is the only thing blocking Accepted status and is already tracked in DECISIONS-r3.md.
findings.fix: No doc change needed. Confirm Q19's re-probe runs before release sign-off; this ADR has no v1-behavior risk to carry forward.

findings.claim: VERDICT for ADR-0015 (apart from the flood-guard.ts blocker above): ACCEPT WITH CORRECTION. The README section plan and file-deletion inventory are sound and match owner decisions (web/ deleted, no npm, Elastic-2.0), but the deletion list mixes files with real fix history (flood-guard.ts, plugin-cache-integrity.ts) into the same DELETE bucket as genuinely dead config/build files, with no per-file archaeology gate before deletion.
findings.evidence: git log --follow --diff-filter=A on src/util/plugin-cache-integrity.ts shows INTRODUCED_BY 9457d436 'feat(adapters/claude-code): doctor surfaces plugin-cache integrity via HealthCheck protocol (algo defense 6 of 6)' -- a named defense layer, not incidental code. ADR-0015's 'Order on v2' section (steps 0-5) sequences deletions by category (removed agents, skills, scripts, package.json, tests/) but does not require checking each file's own fix history first, which is how flood-guard.ts's #769 fix slipped into the DELETE bucket unexamined.
findings.fix: Add a step to the ADR-0015 deletion order: before deleting any src/**/*.ts file (not configs/build artifacts), run `git log --follow -- <file>` and confirm its fix intent is either superseded by a named v2 ADR or genuinely obsolete. Re-check plugin-cache-integrity.ts's doctor-surfaced health check against ADR-0010 (doctor-and-upgrade) for the same gap pattern as flood-guard.ts.
